cards.text: Israel has a brand-new king, and his name is Saul. He's thirty years old when he becomes king, and he reigns over Israel forty-two years. He picks three thousand men of Israel to keep and sends the rest of the troops home.

cards.question: Saul keeps two thousand of those three thousand men with him at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel. Who has the other thousand in Gibeah of Benjamin?

cards.text: Jonathan doesn't waste a minute. He attacks the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines hear about it. Uh-oh.

cards.question: With the Philistines stirred up, Saul blows the ___ throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

cards.text: The news spreads to all Israel: “Saul has attacked an outpost of the Philistines, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines!” Hold on. Jonathan does the attacking and Saul gets the headline? I know that feeling. I stamped a THOUSAND cookies once, and everybody thanked the OVEN.

cards.question: Now the people are summoned to join King Saul. Where do they gather?

cards.text: The Philistines assemble to fight Israel: three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. SAND. On the SEASHORE. Friend, I spent years trying to count the dust in a junk drawer and never finished.

cards.question: The Philistine army sets up camp right at Gilgal, where Saul and the people are gathering.
The Philistines camp at Michmash instead. The men of Israel see they're in danger, and their troops are hard-pressed. What do the men of Israel do?

cards.text: Caves, thickets, rocks, cellars, cisterns. And some Hebrews even cross the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. That's not hiding anymore. That's MOVING.

cards.question: Saul stays at Gilgal, and all his troops there are calm and ready for battle.

cards.text: Saul's troops are quaking at Gilgal, and Saul is waiting on Samuel the prophet. Samuel set a time, and Saul waits seven days for it. Seven DAYS. I've watched grown bakers lose it waiting seven minutes on an oven timer.

cards.question: Seven days pass, and Samuel still hasn't come to Gilgal. What starts happening to Saul's troops?

cards.text: Troops slipping away. Philistines camped at Michmash. Still no Samuel. So Saul makes a call.

cards.question: Saul gives an order at Gilgal. What does he tell them to bring him?

answers.text: A runner to go find Samuel

cards.question: With the offerings brought to him, Saul offers up the ___ offering himself.

cards.text: And just as Saul finishes offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrives. Seven days, friend. Seven. And the man walks in right as Saul's done. Saul goes out to greet him.

cards.question: When Samuel asks, “What have you done?” Saul admits his mistake and asks for forgiveness.

cards.text: Nope. Saul explains himself. The troops were deserting him, Samuel didn't come at the appointed time, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash.

cards.question: Saul tells Samuel he thought the Philistines would come down on him at Gilgal before he had done something. What?

answers.text: Sought the favor of the LORD

cards.text: So, Saul says, he felt compelled to offer the burnt offering. I bet the pressure was real. But Samuel has something to say about it.

cards.question: Samuel tells Saul he has acted ___ and has not kept the ___ the LORD his God gave him.
Samuel says that if Saul had kept the LORD's command, the LORD would have established his kingdom over Israel for all time.

cards.text: But Saul didn't keep it. So now, Samuel says, Saul's kingdom will not endure.

cards.question: Samuel says the LORD has sought someone else and appointed him ruler over His people. Who?

answers.text: A man after His own heart
A man from Saul's own house

cards.text: Then Samuel sets out from Gilgal and goes up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul counts the troops who are still with him.

cards.question: Saul started with three thousand men, and then the troops began deserting. About how many are with Saul now?

cards.text: About six hundred. From three thousand down to SIX HUNDRED. That's a whole lot of folks who suddenly remembered they left the oven on. Saul, his son Jonathan and their troops are staying in Geba of Benjamin.

cards.question: While Saul and Jonathan stay in Geba, the Philistines pack up their camp at Michmash and go home.
The Philistines stay camped at Michmash, and raiders go out of their camp in ___ divisions.

cards.text: One heads toward Ophrah in the land of Shual, one toward Beth-horon, and one down the border road overlooking the Valley of Zeboim. Three groups, three directions. Like sprinkles when I drop the whole jar.

cards.question: Here's the problem for Israel: no blacksmith can be found anywhere in the land. Why not?

answers.text: The Philistines forbade Hebrew swords and spears
The blacksmiths all fled across the Jordan
Saul had sent the blacksmiths back home

cards.text: So whenever Israelites need a plowshare, mattock, axe or sickle sharpened, they have to go down to the Philistines and pay the Philistines' price. Imagine your oven breaks, and the only repairman in town is the guy trying to shut down your bakery.

cards.question: So when the day of battle comes, who among the troops with Saul and Jonathan has a sword or spear?

answers.text: All six hundred of the men

cards.text: A whole army, and two armed men. And a garrison of the Philistines has gone out to the pass at Michmash. We'll leave it right there for now, friend. Trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: Many story cards after the opening card run past 2 sentences. Stop 1 cards 3, 5, 7 and 10; stop 2 cards 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10; and stop 3 cards 3, 6 and 10 each have 3 to 5 sentences or sentence fragments. Stop 1 card 5 has five.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Israel has a brand-new king" says Saul has only just become king. The passage doesn't say how long he has been reigning, and it already has a grown Jonathan leading a thousand men.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Jonathan first appears as the answer on card 2 and in the story on card 3, but nothing says who he is. He isn't called Saul's son until stop 3 card 3 (1 Samuel 13:16).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Jonathan doesn't waste a minute" adds a sense of speed the text doesn't give. Verse 3 says only "Then Jonathan attacked."

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "With the Philistines stirred up" adds a reaction. Verse 3 says only that the Philistines heard about it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Half of stop 1's choice cards are pure discovery: card 2 (Jonathan), card 4 (ram's horn) and card 6 (Gilgal). None of them can be reasoned out from the earlier cards, so most of the stop's choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: "Samuel the prophet" is a fact from outside the passage, but the card cites only 1 Samuel 13:8 and gives no reference for it, such as 1 Samuel 3:20.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card mostly repeats what is already known: troops leaving (answered on card 2), Philistines at Michmash (stop 1) and no Samuel (card 2). The only new part is "So Saul makes a call."

Nothing tells the baker why Saul is waiting on Samuel. There is no mention of 1 Samuel 10:8, where Samuel told Saul to wait seven days until he came to offer the burnt offerings. Without that, the baker can't reason that Saul would call for offerings, and the heart of the passage (why Saul's offering is a problem) goes unexplained.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The right answer is False because Saul explains himself instead of admitting a mistake, and his reply runs through verses 11 and 12. The card cites only 1 Samuel 13:11.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: "Saul started with three thousand men, and then the troops began deserting" links the 3,000 of verse 2 to the 600 of verse 15. The text never makes that link. Saul sent the rest home (v. 2), and then the people were summoned to Gilgal (v. 4).

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "From three thousand down to SIX HUNDRED" makes the same unstated link between the 3,000 chosen men and the 600 counted in verse 15.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke compares raiders deliberately sent out in three divisions to a dropped jar of sprinkles, which scatters by accident in every direction. The core action (a planned split three ways) doesn't match.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The closing line, "We'll leave it right there for now, friend. Trust me, this story's not done.", nearly copies the doc's example line instead of being a new one.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
